notes:
- Spotlight, a wide still for the Library and Home: Both pickers gain one new viewing style. In the Library it draws one title per row as a wide landscape still, with the name, status and progress underneath and the same progress pill on the cover; on Home it draws one wide still per missed sequel, with the title over the art and the quick-add actions in a measured strip below it. It is a real style in both pages, not a label: the grid, the profile list, the loading skeleton, the card preview and the sequels list all branch on it.
- The Library previews show the page they promise: A Big cards or poster-grid preview sized its cover by the poster's own 2:3 ratio, which was taller than the frame - so the caption underneath was pushed out of the picture, and the one thing separating Big cards from Cover wall was missing from both. The cover now takes what the caption leaves, and the caption is measured first. Mosaic's preview gained the hero caption the real hero prints, Grouped covers gained its status counts and per-cover names, and every preview's progress mark is now the same primary-container pill the grid draws instead of a second badge invented for the preview.
- Banners and Tickets grow with the Text setting: Two sequel styles pinned their cards to a fixed height while their contents are text the reader can enlarge. At 175% the banner's title and quick-add strip no longer fit in 190dp, and the ticket's title and button overflowed 132dp, so the control each card exists to offer was the part cut off. Both are now measured by their content: the artwork fills the height the words ask for, and the button stays on the card.
- The Banners preview finally shows its action strip: The style's own description promises a compact action strip, and the real banner draws the quick-add control over its artwork - but the preview stopped at the title and metadata, so it pictured a plain backdrop. It now shows the strip, which is the difference between a banner and a picture.
- The Library view page leads with the preview: Home sequels shows the shape first and the choices underneath; the Library view page did the reverse, asking the reader to compare a wall of names before showing them the one they had. The preview is now above the chips on both pages, the chosen mode's blurb is no longer printed twice (it is the card's subtitle), and the search index finds the page by the word "spotlight". The App layout and Info page tiles also report which one is selected to a screen reader, which until now was said only by a border colour. The miniature diagrams divide out the reader's font scale so a 175% setting cannot inflate them out of their fixed frames; the labels and chips around them still scale normally.
- Filter labels survive the Text size setting: The dashboard's status/filter strip pinned itself to 38dp while its labels are text the reader can enlarge to 175%. At that size the second line of "Upcoming" was cut through the middle, because a fixed height has nowhere to put it. The strip now takes a minimum height and grows with its tallest segment, exactly as the other segmented control already did; every segment stays the same height, and the labels wrap instead of being lost. Its segments also announce themselves as radio buttons rather than tabs, because the control filters a list rather than switching pages.
- The title you were reading survives a rotation: The dashboard kept the open title, the open arriving row and the filter sheet in plain remembered state. The ViewModel survived a configuration change, so the list came back but the id of the sheet did not: rotating the phone closed the page the reader was on, and a filter sheet could vanish while its filters stayed applied. All three now use saved state, so the sheet and its scroll position come back with the list.
- Search fields put the keyboard away: The dashboard's franchise search, the Library's search and the catalogue search all filter as you type, which left the keyboard's action key with nothing to do. Pressing it did not dismiss the keyboard or drop focus, so the results it had just produced stayed half hidden behind it. All three now use the Search action, which closes the keyboard - the same contract the settings and GIF searches already had.
- A blank tier name no longer looks saved: Both rename flows' confirm button accepted an empty field. The view model refuses a blank name by design, so the row closed, the animation finished, and the old name stayed: a control that reports success and did nothing. The button is now disabled while the field is blank, and the keyboard's Done key saves a non-blank name the same way the button does.
- Long names end in an ellipsis instead of being cut: Six places asked for one line and stopped there, and Compose's default is to clip rather than shorten - so a long profile title, studio name, relation label, comment author, schedule pill or comment error message was sliced through a letter with no sign that anything was missing. They all ellipsize now, and the clipped half is still available to a screen reader where the row carries an action label.
- Buttons grow with their labels: The primary action, the sign-in and demo buttons and the setup wizard's Back were pinned to 48-50dp. Their labels are scaled by the app's own Text size setting, and at 175% a one-line label plus the button's padding is taller than the box - so the words were clipped on the screen a first-time reader sees. Each is now a minimum height that can grow, and the pressed pill reads as a softer capsule rather than the label being lost.
- The parent line on a card is a button: The "Sequel to ..." row on every recommendation opens the parent title, and it had an action label but no role. A screen reader therefore never said it was a button, while its only visual feedback was the press scale. It now carries the button role, which is what its tap surface has always been.
